meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?
Where is your room?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'толик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'small table, café table' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: A coffee, please.
Thank you! — You're welcome.
Please see him out.

meanings.note: Indeclinable neuter noun borrowed from French 'menu' (detailed list, from Latin 'minutus').

examples.trans: What's this menu here?
The menu, please.

examples.text: Что за меню здесь? Как позвонить?
examples.trans: What's this menu here? How do I make a call?

передать.gloss: to pass on, to hand over

meanings.en: to pass on, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pass on, to hand over', paired with 'передавать'.

examples.trans: Give this to Alexei.
Please pass on my regards to your mum.

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'head chef, executive chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

examples.text: Они привели нового шеф-повара прямо из Индии.
examples.trans: They brought a new chef straight from India.

examples.text: Шеф-повар решит, подходите ли вы ресторану.
examples.trans: The head chef will decide whether you suit the restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.
Let him say it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'авать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to serve, submit, file'.

examples.text: Как будто ты подаёшь на развод.
examples.trans: As if you are filing for divorce.

examples.text: Подавай мясо на горячей тарелке гостям.
examples.trans: Serve the meat to the guests on a hot plate.

examples.text: Вика, скорее подавай гостям горячие блюда!
examples.trans: Vika, serve the hot dishes to the guests quickly!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('turtle, tortoiseshell').

examples.text: Передайте шеф-повару, пусть подает черепаховый суп, окей?
examples.trans: Tell the head chef to serve the turtle soup, okay?
Your turtle soup.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'soupe' in the Petrine era.

examples.text: Сегодня на кухне сварили вкусный суп.
examples.trans: Today in the kitchen they cooked delicious soup.
I like hot soup very much!

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'okay', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А я пойду принесу выпить, окей?
examples.trans: I will go grab us something to drink, okay?

examples.text: Я уже всё решил. Одну треть на кладбище, две трети над океаном.
examples.trans: I've already sorted it all out. One third goes to the cemetery, two thirds over the ocean.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'five hundred', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It costs five hundred roubles.
About five hundred roubles.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rouble' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This costs a hundred roubles.
I haven't got a single rouble.

examples.text: Наша задача — взять у взяточников миллиард рублей.
examples.trans: Our task is to take a billion roubles from the bribe-takers.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'a hundred', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I need a hundred roubles.
I've got a hundred and ten.

examples.text: Понимаешь, Аркаша, мы все скидываемся на этот кластер. Мне москвичам сегодня надо отдать сто пятьдесят.
examples.trans: You see, Arkasha, we're all chipping in for this cluster. I have to give the Moscow people a hundred and fifty today.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thousand' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That means thousands of jobs.
A thousand roubles.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'ллар'). Common masculine noun meaning 'dollar' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It costs ten thousand dollars!
The ticket costs a hundred dollars.

examples.text: Возьмите! Они десять тысяч долларов стоят!
examples.trans: Take it! It costs ten thousand dollars!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to throw; to abandon', paired with 'бросить'.

examples.trans: Don't hang up!

examples.text: Он всегда бросает вещи на пол.
examples.trans: He always throws things on the floor.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ковородка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'frying pan, skillet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A heavy frying pan was sizzling on the stove.

examples.text: Он быстро снял сковородку с огня.
examples.trans: He quickly took the frying pan off the heat.

examples.text: Во имя тяжёлой сковородки и половника!
examples.trans: In the name of the heavy frying pan and ladle!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Nobody will come in.
I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.
See the markers? They're from Japan!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'который'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('some, certain').

examples.trans: To some, life itself gives a chance.
Some guests ordered dessert.

examples.text: Некоторым сама жизнь даёт второй шанс.
examples.trans: To some, life itself gives a second chance.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'path, way, journey' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here is a movie: A Thorny Path.

examples.text: Давай, счастливого пути и хорошей дороги!
examples.trans: Go ahead, safe travels and have a good road!

examples.text: Ты сам выбрал этот страшный путь.
examples.trans: You chose this terrible path yourself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full, complete, total').

examples.trans: This is a total nightmare!

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ключение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'adventure' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The main adventure is only just beginning!

examples.text: В Москве Макса ждали новые приключения.
examples.trans: New adventures awaited Max in Moscow.

examples.text: И главное приключение ещё только начинается!
examples.trans: And the main adventure is only just beginning!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'miracle, wonder' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a culinary miracle!

examples.text: Потому что это настоящее кулинарное чудо!
examples.trans: Because it is a real culinary miracle!
Just wait for a miracle.

успевать.gloss: to manage in time, have time

meanings.en: to manage in time, have time
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спевать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to manage in time, have time'.

related.gloss: to to manage in time (prefixed perfective)
not to to manage in time (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: We cannot get anything done in time.

examples.text: Повара ничего не успевают вовремя отдавать.
examples.trans: The cooks cannot serve anything on time.

examples.text: Я не успеваю. Это в другую сторону.
examples.trans: I do not have time. That is the other way.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'держаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to resist, refrain, hold back'.

examples.text: Я не удержалась и купила пёсика.
examples.trans: I could not resist and bought a puppy.
Yet by a miracle they manage to hold on.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone, somebody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

оказаться.gloss: to turn out to be, find oneself

meanings.en: to turn out to be, find oneself
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out to be, find oneself', paired with 'оказываться'.

examples.trans: You turned out to be ungrateful.

examples.text: Он внезапно оказался в центре событий.
examples.trans: He suddenly found himself in the center of events.
And you turned out to be an ungrateful woman!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'путье'). Common neuter noun meaning 'crossroads' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А кто-то, оказавшись на перепуте, выбирает направление.
examples.trans: While someone else, standing at a crossroads, chooses a direction.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое перепутье.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new crossroads.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'бирать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to choose, select, pick'.

examples.trans: He takes a long time choosing a new dish.
Always choose the right words.

examples.text: Выбирай слова, когда говоришь с ней!
examples.trans: Choose your words when talking with her!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'правление'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'referral slip; direction' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll write out a referral right now.
Which direction should we walk in?

examples.text: Сейчас выпишу направление. Где я вас могла видеть?
examples.trans: I'll write out a referral right now. Where could I have seen you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'which, who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.
examples.trans: For him to give back the money he stole.

examples.text: Который ему город подарил! И откуда у Аллы Евгеньевны новая шуба!
examples.trans: Which the city donated to him! And where Alla Yevgenyevna got a new fur coat!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'bye', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!
That's it, bye!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'известно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Without knowing yet where it will lead.

examples.text: На кухне все стараются работать неизвестно.
examples.trans: In the kitchen everyone tries to work unknown.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

examples.text: Хорошо. Значит, вот куда идут деньги налогоплательщиков.
examples.trans: Fine. So this is where taxpayers' money goes.

examples.text: Значит, вот куда идут деньги налогоплательщиков.
examples.trans: So this is where taxpayers' money goes.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'везти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning '(they) delivered, brought', paired with 'привозить'.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
I've brought you your things.

examples.text: Плохой бетон привезли. Самсон, ты зря радиаторы носил.
examples.trans: They've delivered bad concrete. Samson, you carried those radiators for nothing.
